metadata.title: Plan Artifact Updates
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Plan specific changes to an existing framework artifact (template, step, or process) by reviewing the update description, loading baseline analysis, prompting for backward compatibility, checking for active consumers, and producing an update-plan.md for approval. Use before applying changes to any artifact.

artifactPath.description: Path to the artifact (relative to project root)

updateDescription.description: Description of what changes are needed
updateDescription.example: Add approval checkpoint after analysis step

changeScope.description: Scope of changes: minor (small fixes) or major (structural changes). If omitted, agent determines from analysis.

preserveActiveConsumers.description: Whether to warn if active consumers use this artifact

output.description: Detailed update plan document for user approval

prerequisites: Artifact has been analyzed by analyze-current-artifact-state (or equivalent)
Analysis baseline (currentStructure) is available in memory.json from prior step
updateDescription is available in process parameters
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: validate params → review requirements → load analysis → prompt compatibility → check consumers → design changes → (Q&A if needed) → create plan → review plan → present for approval
The backward compatibility prompt is the KEY user interaction — log it immediately
Use type-specific change targets and consumer checks (see artifactTypeConfig)
The update-plan.md serves as a contract: the apply step implements exactly what's approved
Do NOT apply changes in this step — only plan them

read: Artifact files for reference during change design
update: memory.json (current step section with plan details)

tools: grep - Search for active consumers (processes using template, templates referencing step)
bestPractices: Always load the baseline analysis before designing changes — never plan from scratch
Log the backward compatibility response immediately (LOG FIRST principle)
Design changes as before/after pairs for clarity
Check for side effects and downstream consequences
Keep the plan document human-readable — it's an approval deliverable
Self-review the plan before presenting to the user
When user requests changes, loop through review again before re-presenting

consumerCheck.description: Search for active processes using this template
consumerCheck.searchPattern: Read process.json files and check metadata.template field

compatibilityConcerns: Removing steps may orphan in-progress work

consumerCheck.description: Search for templates referencing this step
consumerCheck.searchPattern: Search for @framework-step:{category}/{stepName} in template JSON files

compatibilityConcerns: Removing substeps may break templates that depend on specific outputs
Changing output format affects downstream steps
Renaming memory fields breaks steps that read from memory

consumerCheck.searchPattern: Read process.json subProcessState for parent and child references

compatibilityConcerns: Active process instances may be mid-execution
Child processes may depend on parent state
Changing step IDs breaks memory references

substeps.name: Init-Step: Confirm Principles
substeps.description: Recall operating principles before starting this step
actions: Read `.processes/steps/_components/operating-principles.md` and recall all principles
Output: '✓ Principles confirmed for this step'

substeps.name: Validate Parameters
substeps.description: Confirm all required parameters are valid
actions: Confirm `artifactType` is one of: template, step, process
Confirm `artifactPath` is provided and non-empty
Confirm `updateDescription` is provided
If optional parameters are provided, note them
If required parameters are invalid, log error to log.json and stop

substeps.name: Review Update Requirements
actions: Read the `updateDescription` from process parameters
Read any `changeScope` parameter (minor/major) if provided
Understand what changes are requested
Identify the scope and nature of the update

substeps.name: Load Artifact Analysis from Memory
substeps.description: Read the baseline analysis from the prior step
actions: Read the previous step's analysis results from memory.json
This includes the `currentStructure` baseline recorded by `analyze-current-artifact-state`
Build understanding of the current state before planning changes
If analysis is missing or incomplete, log error and stop

substeps.name: Prompt User for Backward Compatibility
substeps.description: Ask the user about backward compatibility requirements
actions: Ask the user: 'Is backward compatibility required for this update?'
Wait for user response
Log the response to log.json IMMEDIATELY (LOG FIRST principle)
Record the decision — it shapes how changes are designed
If yes: changes must not break active consumers (see artifactTypeConfig.compatibilityConcerns)
If no: breaking changes are allowed; full restructuring permitted

substeps.name: Check for Active Consumers
substeps.description: Search for consumers of this artifact based on its type
actions: Based on `artifactType`, check for active consumers using artifactTypeConfig
For templates: search `.user-processes/active/` for processes using this template
For steps: search `.processes/templates/` for templates referencing this step via `@framework-step:{category}/{stepName}`
For processes: check `subProcessState` for parent/child relationships
Report findings to the user
If `preserveActiveConsumers` is true, flag changes that would break consumers

substeps.name: Design Specific Changes
substeps.description: Design each change using type-specific change targets
actions: Based on update description, analysis baseline, backward compatibility decision, and artifact type, design each change
Use type-specific change targets from artifactTypeConfig
For each change, document: what exactly changes (before → after), why the change is needed, impact on existing functionality, whether it's backward compatible
If gaps or ambiguities exist, proceed to Q&A (Substep 7)

substeps.name: Q&A Session (if needed)
substeps.description: Gather missing details from user if gaps found in change design
actions: If any gaps or ambiguities exist in the planned changes, ask the user for clarification
Use the qa-session component pattern
Log user responses to log.json
Return to Substep 6 after gathering answers
Skip this substep if all changes are well-defined

substeps.name: Create update-plan.md
substeps.description: Write the detailed change plan document
actions: Create `update-plan.md` in the process folder

Include sections: Summary, Artifact (type/path/name), Backward Compatibility (decision and implications), Active Consumers (impact assessment), Detailed Changes (each change with before/after, rationale, impact), Files to Modify, Risks and Considerations

substeps.name: Review and Refine Plan
substeps.description: Self-review the plan for quality before presenting to user
actions: Re-read the generated `update-plan.md` critically
Verify completeness: are all requested changes from `updateDescription` addressed?
Verify consistency: do changes align with the backward compatibility decision?
Verify correctness: are before/after descriptions accurate against the baseline analysis?
Check for missed impacts: are there side effects or downstream consequences not captured?
Check for unnecessary changes: is anything included that wasn't requested or needed?
If issues found, revise `update-plan.md` and re-review
Output: '✓ Plan reviewed and verified'

substeps.name: Present Plan for User Approval
substeps.description: Summarize the plan and wait for user to approve or request changes
actions: Present a clear summary of the update plan to the user
Highlight the key changes, backward compatibility decision, and any risks
Reference the full `update-plan.md` for detailed review
This is the approval checkpoint — wait for user response
Log user response to log.json
If approved: proceed to End-Step
If request-changes: log the feedback, apply changes to update-plan.md, loop back to Substep 9 (Review and refine), then re-present

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for user interactions (backward compatibility prompt, Q&A, approval)?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: Do modified process files conform to type definitions? (Principle 7)
Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Validate params → Review requirements → Load analysis → Prompt backward compatibility → Type-specific consumer check → Design changes → (Q&A if needed) → Create plan → Review plan → Present for approval (loop on request-changes) → End

memoryFileUsage.readFrom: Process parameters (artifactType, artifactPath, updateDescription) and previous step's analysis (currentStructure)
fields: Information Produced: backwardCompatibility decision, activeConsumersCheck results, changeDesign details, updatePlanRef path
Decisions Made: Backward compatibility decision, change design choices, scope determination
